title: Ordinary open tensor restriction in compatible additive germ coordinates
statement: Let f:X to S, f prime:X prime to S prime, g:S prime to S and g prime:X prime to X form a cartesian square of schemes. Let V and V prime be opens of S and S prime with V prime contained in g inverse V. Set U=f inverse V and U prime=f prime inverse V prime. Let j:U prime to U commute with the inclusions and g prime, and suppose j, the two restrictions of f and f prime, and g restricted to V prime form a cartesian square. Choose derived categories of sheaves of modules on every scheme. For any cochain complex P of structure-sheaf modules on X, point z of U prime, and integer i, let Q0 be the literal termwise open restriction of P. The four stalk rings and ordinary tensor complexes are those of [def-pc-single-complex-base-change-stalk-condition]. There are isomorphisms eR,eA,eB,eC between the four restricted and ambient stalk rings, commuting with both base stalk maps and both maps to the final stalk ring. There are underlying additive chain isomorphisms alpha of the input stalk complexes and tau of the ordinary tensor complexes. Alpha is semilinear over eA and tau sends c0 tensor q0 to eC(c0) tensor alpha(q0). The restricted tensorStalkIso homology and inverse comparisonStalkHomologyIso, followed by stalk cohomology of [def-pc-single-complex-open-tensor-restriction-iso] and [def-pc-open-derived-additive-stalk-iso], equal the inverse forgetful homology factor, homology of tau, the ambient forgetful homology factor and the ambient tensorStalkIso homology and inverse comparisonStalkHomologyIso. This is exclusively an ordinary tensor-stalk statement and contains no base-derived tensor cohomology model or localized comparison.
